analysis.investment_thesis: A fast-growing small-cap defense supplier (45.8% revenue CAGR) whose reported profits are not showing up as cash — OCF was positive only 1 of the last 4 years and cumulative FCF over 2022-25 is roughly -65 Cr. At a P/E of 73 and P/B of 10.9 you are paying a compounder's price for a working-capital-hungry contract manufacturer; invert, and the downside is severe.
key_strengths: Topline compounding 45.8% CAGR (47→146 Cr) with expanding EBITDA margin (~28% in 2025)
ROCE of 23.6% is genuinely attractive if sustainable at scale
Tailwind from India's defense indigenization; promoter holding solid at 68%
key_risks: Profits ≠ cash: FCF of -29/-43/-8 Cr in FY23-25 despite rising PAT — classic receivables/WIP bloat
Valuation (P/E 73, P/B 10.9) leaves zero margin of safety; any growth stumble = sharp de-rating
Tiny 1,516 Cr market cap with defense-contract lumpiness and single-customer (MoD) dependency risk
red_flags: Operating cash flow negative in 3 of last 4 years while accounting profit grew 3x
FY24 equity jumped 25→126 Cr (IPO/QIP) — growth funded by dilution, not internal accruals
FCF/Net Income ratio deeply negative — earnings quality fails the Munger sniff test
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Invert, always invert. The income statement tells a glowing story — revenue quadrupled, EBITDA margins widened to 28%, ROCE of 23.6%. But the cash flow statement tells the truth: cumulative operating cash flow over FY22-25 is roughly -24 Cr against cumulative net profit of ~59 Cr. That gap is sitting in receivables and inventory, which is the signature of a defense/industrial contractor stretching its balance sheet to book revenue. The FY24 equity infusion (25→126 Cr) bailed out the cash burn, and by FY25 cash is already back down to 3 Cr. This is not a compounding machine; it is a capital-consuming job-shop dressed up with accrual accounting.

At 73x earnings for a 1,500 Cr micro-cap with no moat I can identify — aerospace/defense tier-2 suppliers compete on approvals and price, not brand or switching costs — the price embeds perfection. A great business at a fair price beats this setup every time. I'd want to see three consecutive years of OCF ≥ 80% of net profit, debt under control (currently manageable at 21 Cr), and the multiple halved before this deserves a second look. Pass.
